closeout.reason: The managed-SKU registration handshake is implemented, verified, cleanly reviewed, and delivered for maintainer review as Commerce PR #9.
closeout.summary: Closed the current DinkusKit Commerce v1 track with decisions 020-022 verified: provider-neutral pool registration, permanent Inventory SKU identity, explicit existing-SKU review, and one-time Commerce-title naming with SKU fallback. The earlier Commerce-only Manage Stock disable behavior is also verified. Live provider transport, Configure Inventory UI, existing-pool connect and revalidation, and checkout reservation remain explicitly deferred with their accepted fail-closed requirements preserved. No live Inventory stock mutation, deployment, or production change occurred. The next recommended grill is Inventory-owned atomic register-or-return.

current_focus.summary: The managed-SKU registration slice keeps unmanaged products entirely in Commerce. After Manage Stock is enabled and pool setup is explicitly confirmed, Commerce registers the canonical SKU once at pool scope with logical stock zero and no location balance. Inventory returns a permanent opaque SKU identity while the visible SKU remains the unique pool lookup key. A newly registered Inventory item initializes its display name from the current Commerce Product Title, falling back to the SKU when no title exists; later Inventory and Commerce title changes remain independent. Existing pooled SKUs are never overwritten and continue through the already-locked human review and revalidation path. Set Initial Stock remains a separate location-scoped quantity action. The implementation is limited to the provider-neutral Commerce registration contract, pure state transitions, tests, documentation, and proof; it adds no admin UI, OAuth/discovery, live Inventory transport, stock mutation, checkout, deployment, or production change.

decisions.question: What canonical character and normalization contract does a Commerce SKU use?
decisions.rationale: A small canonical alphabet produces deterministic keys across JavaScript, SQLite, D1, Inventory, logs, receipts, and operator input without locale-sensitive collation or confusable punctuation.

decisions.choice: A canonical SKU is one or more uppercase ASCII alphanumeric segments separated by single hyphens. It starts and ends with A-Z or 0-9 and rejects leading, trailing, or consecutive hyphens.

decisions.choice: Every CreateCatalogItem command carries a stable caller-generated commandId. Store commandId and skuKey as unique fields on the same catalogItems row. The same commandId with the same normalized payload returns the original catalog item; the same commandId with different normalized input returns COMMAND_CONFLICT; different command IDs claiming the same skuKey produce exactly one success and one SKU_CONFLICT. Admin and agent callers reuse commandId after timeout or unknown result.

decisions.rationale: Service bindings provide stable runtime transport without coupling Commerce domain contracts to evolving EmDash UI or OAuth decisions. The persisted binding contains no credentials and no stock truth, so future discovery surfaces can change without changing managed-SKU behavior.

decisions.choice: Preserve the product and canonical SKU in a managed setup-required state that is unavailable for purchase and never falls back to unmanaged stock. Immediately present a setup prompt explaining that Manage Stock requires the DinkusKit Inventory plugin, with a Configure Inventory action that drives pool and default fulfillment-location setup before SKU reconciliation can begin. If the merchant dismisses the prompt, Manage Stock remains checked, the product remains Managed — setup required, and a persistent Configure Inventory action remains visible. The interface must clearly state that unchecking Manage Stock is the explicit way to leave this state and remove the setup-required status and Configure Inventory action.
decisions.deferred_reason: The setup-required state is implemented and persisted, but purchase availability enforcement and the Configure Inventory prompt are not. Carry those accepted UI/runtime requirements into a successor track.

decisions.rationale: This preserves merchant intent, keeps the product fail-closed, provides a durable recovery path, and makes the only exit from Inventory-managed intent explicit rather than allowing dismissal to silently change stock authority.

decisions.choice: Early in store-level configuration, ask: Already have a DinkusKit Inventory pool? A yes answer enters a separate existing-user setup that connects the store to an existing pool, selects its default fulfillment location, and proceeds to SKU reconciliation. A no answer enters first-time setup to create the required pool and default fulfillment location before returning to SKU reconciliation. After either path succeeds, later managed products reuse the store configuration and go directly to SKU reconciliation.
decisions.deferred_reason: First-time versus existing-pool setup routing is accepted product direction but has no admin UI or live pool adapter yet. Defer it intact until that surface exists.

decisions.question: What happens when a merchant unchecks Manage Stock after the Commerce product is already connected to Inventory?
decisions.rationale: The checkbox controls Commerce product behavior, not shared Inventory ownership. Non-destructive disablement protects pool truth and fresh reconciliation prevents stale assumptions on re-entry.

decisions.choice: Adding a product to a cart does not reserve or mutate Inventory. When the customer selects Place Order, Commerce sends one idempotent request for Inventory to atomically reserve all managed line-item quantities for a limited time. Inventory is the sole authority that either creates the reservation or rejects it for insufficient availability, so only one concurrent checkout can reserve the final unit. A failed checkout or expired reservation releases the held quantity. The reservation duration is a separate decision.
decisions.deferred_reason: Checkout and atomic reservation remain intentionally outside the current managed-SKU foundation. Preserve this accepted boundary for the later checkout track.

decisions.question: What exact code and proof belong in the first Commerce managed-stock foundation PR?
decisions.rationale: This is the smallest reviewable Commerce-owned foundation that makes the product contract durable while keeping evolving Inventory transport, EmDash UI, and OAuth decisions behind replaceable boundaries.

decisions.choice: Register a managed SKU once in the selected Inventory pool, independent of any location, with logical stock at zero. Registration establishes pool-wide SKU identity only: it creates no stock mutation, balance, or receipt. Every active location presents explicit zero for the registered SKU until stock exists. Commerce retains the store default fulfillment-location binding separately and uses that location only when a later Set Initial Stock action is confirmed. Stores sharing the pool reuse the same registered SKU identity.

decisions.question: At what scope does Inventory register a Commerce-managed SKU, and when does location-specific stock begin?
decisions.rationale: Separating pool-wide SKU identity from location balances prevents duplicate product identities per location, preserves stock receipts for real quantity changes, and lets multiple stores and locations share one authoritative pool record.

decisions.choice: Inventory mints one permanent opaque inventory SKU ID when the pool-wide SKU is registered. The human-visible canonical SKU is a unique lookup key within that pool, not the permanent record identity. An explicit confirmed rename may change the visible SKU while retaining the same Inventory SKU ID, balances, and complete history. Receipts preserve the visible SKU snapshot used when each mutation committed. A connected store cannot silently rename a shared pool SKU, and a rename that collides with another registered SKU fails closed.

decisions.question: What happens to Inventory identity and history when a canonical SKU is corrected?
decisions.rationale: A stable hidden identity lets merchants correct a visible SKU without losing stock or breaking receipt history, while explicit confirmation and pool-wide uniqueness protect stores that share the Inventory record.

decisions.choice: When a Commerce product is connected to Inventory for managed stock, a newly registered pooled SKU initializes its Inventory display name from the current Commerce Product Title. If the Commerce product has no title, Inventory temporarily displays the canonical SKU until an authorized Inventory administrator supplies a name. The initial value is a one-time default: later Commerce or storefront title changes do not rename Inventory, another store connecting the pooled SKU does not overwrite it, and an explicit Inventory rename does not change any connected Commerce admin or storefront title. Set Initial Stock remains a separate location-scoped quantity action and does not own naming.

history.choice: The first Commerce store that successfully commits Set Initial Stock for a registered pooled SKU supplies its current Commerce Product Title as the initial Inventory display name. That name then belongs to the Inventory pool record. Other stores may connect the same pooled SKU while keeping different Commerce and storefront titles; those titles never rename Inventory. An authorized Inventory administrator may explicitly rename the Inventory display name without changing any connected Commerce admin title, storefront title, permanent Inventory SKU ID, balance, or history.

When a Commerce product is connected to Inventory for managed stock, a newly registered pooled SKU initializes its Inventory display name from the current Commerce Product Title. If the Commerce product has no title, Inventory temporarily displays the canonical SKU until an authorized Inventory administrator supplies a name. The initial value is a one-time default: later Commerce or storefront title changes do not rename Inventory, another store connecting the pooled SKU does not overwrite it, and an explicit Inventory rename does not change any connected Commerce admin or storefront title. Set Initial Stock remains a separate location-scoped quantity action and does not own naming.

decisions.question: Who owns the Inventory display name for a pooled SKU, and how is its initial value chosen?
decisions.rationale: Commerce already owns the product title before stock management begins, so using it at registration gives Inventory a useful operational name without delaying naming until a stock mutation. One-time initialization plus independent later ownership preserves each storefront title and prevents shared-pool stores from renaming one another.

alternatives: Persist Commerce managed-stock setup transitions with an explicit idempotent command after Inventory exposes the registration operation.
Design the EmDash Configure Inventory setup UI around the now-typed setup-required, needs-review, and active states without adding live transport yet.
recommendation.reason: Commerce now has a verified provider-neutral handshake, but a live cross-stack proof cannot exist until Inventory can atomically create or return the pool-wide SKU identity. That operation is the narrowest dependency and can be built without deciding OAuth or EmDash plugin transport.
recommendation.recommended: Implement Inventory-owned atomic register-or-return for one pool-wide canonical SKU, minting the permanent inventorySkuId and preserving the first displayNameIfNew without creating balances or receipts.
